[经] 询价, 询盘
examples: We received over 300 enquiries about the job.
Greetings and enquiries about family members tend to be in the local dialect.
I'll have to make a few enquiries (= try to find out about it) and get back to you.
definition: n an instance of questioning
n a search for knowledge

enrich.meaning: vt. 使富足, 使肥沃
examples: The study of science has enriched all our lives.
Most breakfast cereals are enriched with vitamins.
He used his position to enrich himself.
definition: v. make better or improve in quality
v. make wealthy or richer

enroll.meaning:
vt. 登记, 使加入
vi. 参军, 注册
examples: I enrolled for/in/on the modern art course.
He is enrolled as a part-time student.
They want to enroll their children in their local school.
definition: v. register formally as a participant or member

ensue.meaning:
vi. 跟着发生, 继起
vt. 追求
examples: An argument ensued.
The riot police swooped in and chaos ensued.
The police officer said that he had placed the man under arrest and that a scuffle had ensued.
definition: v issue or terminate (in a specified way, state, etc.); end

ensure.meaning:
vt. 确定, 保证, 担保, 保护
[经] 确保, 确定
examples: We are working to ensure the safety of people in the city.
The book ensured his success.
We must take steps now to ensure the survival of these animals.
definition: v make certain of
v be careful or certain to do something; make certain of something

entail.meaning:
vt. 使成为必需, 需要, 使承担, 遗传给
n. 限定继承
examples: The job entails a lot of hard work.
The girls learn exactly what is entailed in caring for a newborn baby.
It will entail driving a long distance every day.
definition: n. land received by fee tail
n. the act of entailing property; the creation of a fee tail from a fee simple

enter.meaning:
vt. 进入, 参加, 开始, 输入, 回车
vi. 进去, 参加
[计] 输入, 回车
examples: Knock before you enter.
Enter Hamlet (= for example as stage directions in the text of a play).
Someone entered the room behind me.
definition: v. to come or go into
v. become a participant; be involved in

entire.meaning:
n. 整个, 全部
a. 全体的, 完全的, 全部的
examples: The entire village was destroyed.
You two are her favourite people in the entire world.
The film is perfect for the entire family.
definition: s. constituting the full quantity or extent; complete
s. (of leaves or petals) having a smooth edge; not broken up into teeth or lobes

entirely.meaning: adv. 完全, 全然, 一概
examples: The experience was entirely new to me.
That's an entirely different matter.
We're not entirely sure what to do next.
definition: r. without any others being included or involved

entirety.meaning:
n. 全部, 整体
[法] 共有制, 整体, 全部
examples: The poem is too long to quote in its entirety.
I've never actually read the book in its entirety.
I never read the contract in its entirety, just parts of it.
definition: n. the state of being total and complete

entitle.meaning:
vt. 给...权利, 取名为, 给予名称, 叫做
[法] 给...权利, 使有资格, 称呼
examples: You will be entitled to your pension when you reach 65.
Everyone's entitled to their own opinion.
This ticket does not entitle you to travel first class.
definition: v. give the right to
v. give a title to

entity.meaning:
n. 实体, 实存物, 存在
[计] 实体
examples: The unit has become part of a larger department and no longer exists as a separate entity.
These countries can no longer be viewed as a single entity.
Hip hop is a major commercial entity now (= it is a business, not just a type of music).
definition: n. that which is perceived or known or inferred to have its own distinct existence (living or nonliving)

entrance.meaning:
n. 入口, 进入点, 入场, 入学, 进入, 开始(阶段), 就任
vt. 使出神, 使入迷
[计] 入口
examples: There are two entrances - one at the front and one around the back.
He makes a spectacular entrance in act two draped in a gold sheet.
I noticed her entrance because she slipped and fell in the doorway.
definition: n. something that provides access (to get in or get out)
n. a movement into or inward

entrust.meaning:
vt. 信托, 交托, 委托
[经] 委托
examples: He entrusted the task to his nephew.
The rebuilding of London's churches was entrusted to the brilliant young architect, Christopher Wren.
His mother entrusted him to doctors at Charing Cross hospital.
definition: v. confer a trust upon
v. put into the care or protection of someone

entry.meaning:
n. 登录, 条目, 进入, 入口, 报关
[计] 登录项, 输入项, 条目
examples: She made her entry to the sound of thunderous applause.
The children were surprised by the sudden entry of their teacher.
They block the entry of the HIV virus into the cells.
definition: n. an item inserted in a written record
n. a written record of a commercial transaction

envelop.meaning:
vt. 包封, 遮盖, 包围
n. 信封
examples: She was enveloped in a huge white towel.
Clouds enveloped the mountain tops.
Darkness fell and enveloped the town.
definition: v. enclose or enfold completely with or as if with a covering

envelope.meaning:
n. 信封, 封套, 封袋
[医] 膜, 包袋
examples: Writing paper and envelopes are provided in your room.
Each item was tagged and sealed in a plastic envelope.
We added up our savings on the back of an envelope.
definition: n. a flat (usually rectangular) container for a letter, thin package, etc.
n. any wrapper or covering

envious.meaning: a. 嫉妒的, 羡慕的
examples: Everyone is so envious of her.
They were envious of his success.
He saw the envious look in the other boy's eyes.
definition: s showing extreme cupidity; painfully desirous of another's advantages

envisage.meaning: vt. 面对, 正视, 想象
examples: I can't envisage her coping with this job.
I don't envisage working with him again.
It is envisaged that the talks will take place in the spring.
definition: v form a mental image of something that is not present or that is not the case

envoy.meaning:
n. 外交使节, 特使
[法] 使者, 代表, 使节
examples: The President has suggested sending a US peace envoy to the Middle East.
definition: n. a diplomat having less authority than an ambassador
n. a brief stanza concluding certain forms of poetry

envy.meaning:
n. 羡慕, 嫉妒
vt. 羡慕, 嫉妒
examples: He couldn't conceal his envy of me.
She felt a pang of envy at the thought of his success.
They looked with envy at her latest purchase.
definition: n. a feeling of grudging admiration and desire to have something that is possessed by another
n. spite and resentment at seeing the success of another (personified as one of the deadly sins)

epic.meaning:
n. 史诗, 叙事诗
a. 史诗的, 叙事诗的
examples: Their four-hour match on Centre Court was an epic.
It's one of those old Hollywood epics with a cast of thousands.
The problem of inflation has reached epic proportions.
definition: s. very imposing or impressive; surpassing the ordinary (especially in size or scale)
a. constituting or having to do with or suggestive of a literary epic

epidemic.meaning:
n. 传染病, 流行病
a. 流行的, 传染性的
examples: An epidemic of measles broke out, and over 200 children died.
Effectively, tobacco companies will be exporting an epidemic of smoking-related diseases, the campaign suggests.
A recent report describes an epidemic of crime in the inner cities.
definition: n. a widespread outbreak of an infectious disease; many people are infected at the same time
a. (especially of medicine) of disease or anything resembling a disease; attacking or affecting many individuals in a community or a population simultaneously

episode.meaning:
n. 插曲, 插话, 有趣的事件, 一段情节
[医] 插话, 插曲, 发作
examples: The next episode has not yet been filmed.
I watched a few episodes of seasons one and two.
The soap opera is ending after 175 episodes.
definition: n. a happening that is distinctive in a series of related events
n. a brief section of a literary or dramatic work that forms part of a connected series

epoch.meaning: n. 新纪元, 时代, 时期
examples: The death of the emperor marked the end of an epoch in the country's history.
The president said that his country was moving into a new epoch, which would be one of lasting peace.
Scientists discovered remains of wooly mammoths and mastodons believed to be from the Pleistocene epoch, more than 10,000 years ago.
definition: n. (astronomy) an arbitrarily fixed date that is the point in time relative to which information (as coordinates of a celestial body) is recorded
n. a unit of geological time that is a subdivision of a period and is itself divided into ages

equal.meaning:
n. 对手, 匹敌, 同辈
a. 相等的, 平等的, 胜任的, 合适的, 平静的, 不相上下的
vt. 等于, 比得上
[计] 等长度编码
examples: There is an equal number of boys and girls in the class.
Each side will put in an equal amount of money.
Cut it into four equal parts.
definition: v. be identical or equivalent to
v. be equal to in quality or ability

equality.meaning:
n. 平等, 均匀, 相等
[法] 同等, 平等, 相等
examples: We need to ensure equality of opportunity in all areas of work.
She works as an adviser on equality and diversity at the Institute of Personnel and Development.
We want to see equality and justice in the workplace.
definition: n. the quality of being the same in quantity or measure or value or status
n. a state of being essentially equal or equivalent; equally balanced

equally.meaning: adv. 相等地, 同样地, 平等地
examples: Diet and exercise are equally important.
This job could be done equally well by a computer.
Everyone should be treated equally.
definition: r. to the same degree (often followed by `as')

equate.meaning:
vt. 使相等, 视为平等
vi. 等同
examples: Some parents equate education with exam success.
I don't see how you can equate the two things.
He complained that there was a tendency to equate right-wing politics with self-interest.
definition: v. be equivalent or parallel, in mathematics

equation.meaning:
n. 相等, 等式, 平衡
[化] 方程式; 等式; 反应式; 公式
examples: The equation of wealth with happiness can be dangerous.
When children enter the equation, further tensions may arise within a marriage.
Money also comes into the equation.
definition: n. a mathematical statement that two expressions are equal
n. the act of regarding as equal

equator.meaning:
n. 赤道
[医] 赤道, 中纬线
examples: The island is twenty degrees south of the equator.
Indonesia is/lies on the equator.
definition: n. an imaginary line around the Earth forming the great circle that is equidistant from the north and south poles
n. a circle dividing a sphere or other surface into two usually equal and symmetrical parts

equip.meaning:
vt. 装备, 配备
[机] 设备, 装置
examples: She got a bank loan to rent and equip a small workshop.
He equipped himself with a street plan.
The centre is well equipped for canoeing and mountaineering.
definition: v. provide with (something) usually for a specific purpose
v. provide with abilities or understanding

equity.meaning:
n. 公平, 公正
[经] 权益, 产权
examples: He plans to raise the company's return on equity to 15%.
The couple have no savings except for the equity in their house.
The rules of common law and equity are both, in essence, systems of private law.
definition: n. the difference between the market value of a property and the claims held against it
n. the ownership interest of shareholders in a corporation

era.meaning: n. 时代, 纪元, 时期
examples: When she left the firm, it was the end of an era (= things were different after that).
This is the start of a new era of peace and prosperity.
They had worked for peace during the long era of conflict.
definition: n. a period marked by distinctive character or reckoned from a fixed point or event
n. a major division of geological time; an era is usually divided into two or more periods

erase.meaning:
vt. 抹去, 擦掉
[计] 清洗; 擦除; 抹除; DOS内部命令:从磁盘上删除一个或多个文件
examples: She tried to erase the memory of that evening.
All doubts were suddenly erased from his mind.
You cannot erase injustice from the world.
definition: v. remove from memory or existence
v. remove by or as if by rubbing or erasing

examples: If you draw or write in pencil you can always rub out your mistakes with an eraser.
definition: n. an implement used to erase something

erect.meaning:
a. 直立的, 竖立的, 笔直的
vt. 使竖立, 使直立, 树立, 建立
vi. 勃起
examples: The church was erected in 1582.
Police had to erect barriers to keep crowds back.
The war memorial was erected in 1950.
definition: a. upright in position or posture

erection.meaning:
n. 直立, 竖起, 建筑物
[化] 装配
examples: The cafe was a bleak, concrete erection with plastic tables and chairs.
They approved the erection of an electric fence around the prison.
This splendid if extraordinary erection from the last century is a local landmark.
definition: n. an erect penis
n. a structure that has been erected

erode.meaning:
vt. 腐蚀, 侵蚀
vi. 受腐蚀
examples: The cliff face has been steadily eroded by the sea.
The rocks have eroded away over time.
Her confidence has been slowly eroded by repeated failures.
definition: v. become ground down or deteriorate
v. remove soil or rock

erosion.meaning:
n. 腐蚀, 冲蚀, 侵蚀
[化] 磨耗; 侵蚀
examples: Many see these security measures as an erosion of civil liberties.
The survey reveals a gradual erosion of the president's popularity and support.
Investors may have seen some erosion of capital over the year.
definition: n. (geology) the mechanical process of wearing or grinding something down (as by particles washing over it)
n. condition in which the earth's surface is worn away by the action of water and wind

err.meaning:
vi. 犯错, 做错, 犯罪
[法] 弄错, 犯错误, 陈述
examples: I thought it was better to err on the side of caution (= to be too careful rather than take a risk).
He erred in agreeing to her appointment to the position.
It's preferable to err on the side of caution (= to be too careful) rather than risk disaster.
definition: v. to make a mistake or be incorrect

errand.meaning: n. 任务, 差使, 使命
examples: He often runs errands for his grandmother.
Her boss sent her on an errand into town.
I'll meet you at six, I have some errands to do/run first.
definition: n. a short trip that is taken in the performance of a necessary task or mission

error.meaning:
n. 错误, 过失, 失误, 误差
[计] 错误
examples: The report contains some factual errors that must be corrected.
They committed the fatal error of misjudging the weather conditions.
There are too many errors in your work.
definition: n. a misconception resulting from incorrect information
n. (baseball) a failure of a defensive player to make an out when normal play would have sufficed

erupt.meaning:
vi. 爆发
vt. 喷出
examples: The volcano could erupt at any time.
Ash began to erupt from the crater.
An immense volume of rocks and molten lava was erupted.
definition: v. start abruptly
v. erupt or intensify suddenly

eruption.meaning:
n. 爆发, 喷出物, 出疹
[化] 喷发
examples: Around the year 600, the eruption of a nearby volcano buried Ceren's buildings.
There was a violent eruption of anti-government feeling.
The curfew was aimed at preventing any eruption of violence in the capital.
definition: n. symptom consisting of a breaking out and becoming visible
n. (of volcanos) pouring out fumes or lava (or a deposit so formed)

escalate.meaning:
vi. 逐步扩大, 逐步升高, 逐步增强
vt. 使逐步上升
examples: The fighting escalated into a full-scale war.
We do not want to escalate the war.
His financial problems escalated after he became unemployed.
definition: v. increase in extent or intensity

escape.meaning:
n. 逃亡, 避难设备, 逃跑
vi. 逃脱, 避开, 溜走
vt. 逃避, 避免, 被...忘掉
examples: Two prisoners have escaped.
They were caught trying to escape.
He escaped from prison this morning.
definition: n. the act of escaping physically
n. an inclination to retreat from unpleasant realities through diversion or fantasy

escort.meaning:
n. 护送者, 护卫者, 护航舰
vt. 护卫, 护送
examples: Armed escorts are provided for visiting heads of state.
Prisoners are taken to court under police escort.
The convoy had an escort of ten destroyers.
definition: n. the act of accompanying someone or something in order to protect them
n. an attendant who is employed to accompany someone

essay.meaning:
n. 随笔, 短文, 评论, 企图
vt. 试图
examples: I have to write an essay this weekend.
He made some very good points in his essay.
The book contains a number of interesting essays on women in society.
definition: n. an analytic or interpretive literary composition
n. a tentative attempt

essence.meaning:
n. 实质, 本质, 香精
[化] 香精
examples: His paintings capture the essence of France.
In essence (= when you consider the most important points), your situation isn't so different from mine.
In this situation time is of the essence (= we must do things as quickly as possible).
definition: n. any substance possessing to a high degree the predominant properties of a plant or drug or other natural product from which it is extracted

estate.meaning:
n. 不动产, (人生的)阶段, 阶层, 财产
[经] 房地产, 遗产, 财产
examples: She lives in a tower block on an estate in London.
The poet's childhood was spent on a country estate.
She receives rent from all the people whose cottages are on estate land.
definition: n. everything you own; all of your assets (whether real property or personal property) and liabilities
n. extensive landed property (especially in the country) retained by the owner for his own use

esteem.meaning:
n. 尊敬, 尊重
vt. 尊敬, 尊重, 认为
examples: She is held in high esteem by her colleagues.
Over the years, he has earned our affection and esteem.
Please accept this small gift as a token of our esteem.
definition: n. the condition of being honored (esteemed or respected or well regarded)

estimate.meaning:
n. 估计, 判断
vt. 估计, 评价, 判断
vi. 估计
examples: The satellite will cost an estimated £400 million.
Police estimate the crowd at 30 000.
All variables can be estimated from the data.
definition: n. an approximate calculation of quantity or degree or worth
n. a judgment of the qualities of something or somebody

eternal.meaning: a. 永恒的, 永远的, 不灭的
examples: She's an eternal optimist (= she always expects that the best will happen).
You have my eternal gratitude (= very great gratitude).
To his eternal credit (= very great credit), he never gave up.
definition: s continuing forever or indefinitely
s tiresomely long; seemingly without end

eternity.meaning: n. 永远, 来世, 不朽
examples: There will be rich and poor for all eternity.
They believed that their souls would be condemned to burn in hell for eternity.
After what seemed like an eternity the nurse returned with the results of the test.
definition: n. time without end
n. a state of eternal existence believed in some religions to characterize the afterlife

ethic.meaning: n. 道德规范, 伦理
examples: He began to question the ethics of his position.
The ethic of personal achievement is very strong in western societies.
The ethics of journalism are much debated.
definition: n. the principles of right and wrong that are accepted by an individual or a social group
n. a system of principles governing morality and acceptable conduct

ethics.meaning:
n. 道德规范
[医] 伦理学
examples: They're completely lacking in ethics.
definition: n. the philosophical study of moral values and rules

ethnic.meaning:
a. 人种的, 种族的
[医] 人种的
examples: Our government should reflect the racial and ethnic diversity of our country.
The country is divided along ethnic lines.
A question on ethnic origin was included in the census.
definition: n. a person who is a member of an ethnic group

euro.meaning: n. 欧元（欧盟的统一货币单位）
examples: I paid five euros for it.
The price is given in euros.
A half-kilo pack of pasta costs around 70 euro cents.
definition: n. the basic monetary unit of most members of the European Union (introduced in 1999); in 2002 twelve European nations (Germany, France, Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Ireland, Greece, Austria, Finland) adopted the euro as their basic unit of money and abandoned their traditional currencies

european.meaning:
n. 欧洲人
a. 欧洲的, 欧洲人的
examples: A slowdown in European growth has prompted investors to switch away from the euro.
definition: n. a native or inhabitant of Europe
a. of or relating to or characteristic of Europe or the people of Europe

evacuate.meaning: v. 疏散, 撤出, 排泄
examples: Police evacuated nearby buildings.
Children were evacuated from London to escape the bombing.
Families were evacuated to safer parts of the city.
definition: v. move out of an unsafe location into safety
v. empty completely

evade.meaning: v. (巧妙地)逃脱, 规避, 逃避
examples: For two weeks they evaded the press.
He managed to evade capture.
They narrowly evaded a police car which was approaching.
definition: v. practice evasion
v. use cunning or deceit to escape or avoid

evaluate.meaning: vt. 评估, 评价, 赋值
examples: The trial will evaluate the effectiveness of the different drugs.
Researchers evaluated teaching performance by comparing students' exam results.
The study will critically evaluate whether this technology is useful.
definition: v. form a critical opinion of

evasion.meaning:
n. 逃避, 藉口
[法] 回避, 规避, 逃避
examples: His behaviour was an evasion of his responsibilities as a father.
She's been charged with tax evasion.
His speech was full of evasions and half-truths.
definition: n. a statement that is not literally false but that cleverly avoids an unpleasant truth
n. the deliberate act of failing to pay money

evasive.meaning:
a. 逃避的, 回避的, 托辞的
[法] 逃避的, 规避的, 推托的
examples: Tessa was evasive about why she had not been at home that night.
John, normally so honest, was now being evasive in the extreme.
The pilot had to take evasive action to avoid a mid-air collision.
definition: s. deliberately vague or ambiguous
s. avoiding or escaping from difficulty or danger especially enemy fire

examples: Mrs. Clayton was speaking to Arab journalists in Paris on the eve of her visit to Egypt.
definition: n. (Old Testament) Adam's wife in Judeo-Christian mythology: the first woman and mother of the human race; God created Eve from Adam's rib and placed Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden
n. the day before

even.meaning:
a. 平坦的, 相等的, 连贯的, 均等的, 公平的, 偶数的, 平均的, 平衡的, 恰好的
vt. 使平坦, 使相等
vi. 变平, 成为相等
adv. 甚至, 实际上, 完全, 十分
n. 偶数, 偶校验
[计] 偶数, 偶校验
examples: She didn't even call to say she wasn't coming.
He never even opened the letter (= so he certainly didn't read it).
It wouldn't have been possible 30 years ago, maybe even 20.
definition: v. become even or more even
v. make even or more even

evening.meaning: n. 傍晚, 晚间, 末期
examples: Remember to call me this evening.
We haven't spoken to him since yesterday evening.
I'll see you tomorrow evening.
definition: n. the latter part of the day (the period of decreasing daylight from late afternoon until nightfall)
n. a later concluding time period

evenly.meaning: adv. 平衡地, 平坦地, 平等地
examples: Make sure the paint covers the surface evenly.
She was fast asleep, breathing evenly.
Arrange the tomato slices evenly on the top.
definition: r. in equal amounts or shares; in a balanced or impartial way
r. in a level and regular way

event.meaning:
n. 事件, 结果, 事情的进程, 竞赛项目
[计] 事件
examples: The tragic events of last Monday occurred only 200 metres from the shore.
Historians long ago established that the event never happened.
TV viewers watched in horror as events unfolded.
definition: n. something that happens at a given place and time
n. a special set of circumstances

eventful.meaning: a. 变故多的, 多事的, 重要的
examples: It had been a long and eventful journey.
Her time at college was the most eventful period of her life.
We had quite an eventful trip.
definition: a. full of events or incidents

eventual.meaning: a. 最后的, 终于的
examples: It is impossible to predict what the eventual outcome will be.
The village school may face eventual closure.
The Dukes were the eventual winners of the competition.
definition: s. expected to follow in the indefinite future from causes already operating

ever.meaning: adv. 曾经, 究竟, 永远
examples: Nothing ever happens here.
If you're ever in Miami, come and see us.
She hardly ever (= almost never) goes out.
definition: r. at any time
r. (intensifier for adjectives) very

examples: She knows every student in the school.
I could hear every word they said.
We enjoyed every minute of our stay.
definition: s. (used of count nouns) each and all of the members of a group considered singly and without exception
s. each and all of a series of entities or intervals as specified

everyday.meaning: a. 每天的, 日常的, 平常的
examples: Change is a part of everyday life in business.
Using everyday objects, basic scientific principles can be explained to young children.
Violent crime is part of the everyday experience of the people in these neighbourhoods.
definition: s. found in the ordinary course of events
s. commonplace and ordinary

everyone.meaning:
pron. 每个人, 人人
[计] 系统中的一个组名
examples: Everyone cheered and clapped.
Everyone has a chance to win.
Everyone brought their partner to the party.
definition: n. Everybody; -- commonly separated, every one.

evidence.meaning:
n. 根据, 证据, 迹象
[经] 证据, 凭证
examples: Researchers have found clear scientific evidence of a link between exposure to sun and skin cancer.
There is a growing body of evidence for the existence of black holes that are ten times as massive as the Sun.
There is not a shred of evidence that the meeting actually took place.
definition: n. your basis for belief or disbelief; knowledge on which to base belief
n. an indication that makes something evident

vt. 使烦恼, 使焦虑, 使苦恼, 困扰, 折磨, 撕咬
vi. 烦恼, 担心, 撕咬
examples: Don't worry. We have plenty of time.
Stop worrying, Dad—it'll be fine.
Don't worry about me. I'll be all right.

v. be worried, concerned, anxious, troubled, or uneasy

worse.meaning:
n. 更坏的事, 更恶劣的事, 败局

adv. 更坏地, 更恶劣地
examples: The rooms were awful and the food was worse.
The weather got worse during the day.
I've been to far worse places.
definition: n. something inferior in quality or condition or effect
a. (comparative of `bad') inferior to another in quality or condition or desirability

worship.meaning:
n. 崇拜, 礼拜, 尊敬
vi. 参加礼拜
vt. 崇拜, 尊敬
examples: The tradition of ancestor worship stretches back thousands of years.
What she feels for him is akin to worship.
On the island the people worshipped different gods.
definition: n. the activity of worshipping
n. a feeling of profound love and admiration

worst.meaning:
n. 最坏, 最坏的时候
a. 最坏的, 最恶劣的, 最不利的
adv. 最坏, 最糟
examples: It was by far the worst speech he had ever made.
It's not the worst idea I've ever heard.
What she said confirmed my worst fears (= proved they were right).

n. the greatest damage or wickedness of which one is capable

worth.meaning:
n. 价值, 财产
a. 值...的, 值得的
examples: Our house is worth about £100 000.
It isn't worth much.
If you answer this question correctly, it's worth five points.
definition: n. an indefinite quantity of something having a specified value
n. the quality that renders something desirable or valuable or useful

worthy.meaning:
n. 杰出人物
a. 有价值的, 可敬的, 值得的
examples: Very few of his ideas are worthy of further attention.
A number of the report's findings are worthy of note.
No composer was considered worthy of the name until he had written an opera.
definition: n. an important, honorable person (word is often used humorously)
a. having worth or merit or value; being honorable or admirable

examples: I'd love a coffee.
I'd be only too glad to help.
I'd hate you to think I was criticizing you.
definition: imp. of Will
v. t. Commonly used as an auxiliary verb, either in the past

wound.meaning:
n. 创伤, 伤口, 伤疤, 伤害, 痛苦
vt. 伤害, 损害, 使受伤
vi. 打伤, 伤害

She refuses to talk about the incident, saying it would only reopen old wounds (= make her remember unhappy past experiences).

n. a casualty to military personnel resulting from combat

wow.meaning:
interj. (非正式)哇
n. 巨大的成功, 轰动一时的成功, 十分有趣的事物

wrap.meaning:
n. 外套, 围巾, 包裹物, 限制, 约束, 秘密, 换行
vt. 包装, 卷, 缠绕, 包, 裹, 覆盖, 遮蔽, 隐藏, 掩护
vi. 缠绕, 穿外衣, 包起来
[计] 换行
examples: He spent the evening wrapping up the Christmas presents.
Each apple was wrapped in paper.
The cheese is cut and wrapped in plastic.

n. a sandwich in which the filling is rolled up in a soft tortilla

wrapping.meaning:
n. 用于包裹的材料
[计] 绕接
examples: She tore the cellophane wrapping off the box.
The painting was still in its wrappings.
The dress still hung in its plastic wrappings.
definition: n. the covering (usually paper or cellophane) in which something is wrapped

wreath.meaning:
n. 花圈, 花环, 圈状物
[医] 花冠, 花冠体(细胞核分裂的一时期)

The bride wore a veil with a wreath of silk flowers.
There were two large wreaths on the coffin.
definition: n. flower arrangement consisting of a circular band of foliage or flowers for ornamental purposes

wreck.meaning:
n. 失事, 残骸, 破坏
vt. 使失事, 拆毁, 破坏
vi. (船)失事, 营救失事船只
examples: They're going to try and raise the wreck from the seabed.
Two passengers are still trapped in the wreck.
She was pulled from the burning wreck by firefighters.
definition: n. something or someone that has suffered ruin or dilapidation

wreckage.meaning:
n. 残骸, 失事, 破坏
[经] (船双等的)失事遭难
examples: A few survivors were pulled from the wreckage.
Pieces of wreckage were found ten miles away from the scene of the explosion.

wrench.meaning:
n. 扳钳, 扳手, 扭伤, 歪曲, 痛苦

vi. 猛扭, 猛绞
examples: The bag was wrenched from her grasp.
He grabbed Ben, wrenching him away from his mother.
Guy wrenched his mind back to the present.
definition: n. a sharp strain on muscles or ligaments
n. a hand tool that is used to hold or twist a nut or bolt

wrestle.meaning:
n. 摔跤, 角力, 扭斗
vi. 摔跤, 搏斗, 斗争, 斟酌
vt. 与(对手)摔跤
examples: As a boy he had boxed and wrestled.
Armed guards wrestled with the intruder.
She tried to wrestle with her attacker.

v. combat to overcome an opposing tendency or force

wretched.meaning: a. 可怜的, 不幸的, 卑鄙的
examples: I felt wretched about the way things had turned out.
She looked thoroughly wretched.
She had a wretched time of it at school.
definition: s of very poor quality or condition
s characterized by physical misery

wrinkle.meaning:
n. 皱纹, 妙计, 方法, 技巧
vi. 起皱
vt. 使起皱纹

I tried to iron out the wrinkles in my shirt.

n. a minor difficulty

wrist.meaning:
n. 手腕, 腕关节
[医] 腕

He wore a copper bracelet on his wrist.
We're hoping that she gets off with a slap on the wrist from the judge.

write.meaning:
vt. 书写, 著述, 写, 写满, 写信给

Please write in pen on both sides of the paper.
I haven't got anything to write with.

writer.meaning:
n. 作家, 撰稿者, 抄写员
[化] 记录器

I used to be a prolific letter writer.
She is a well-known writer of children's books.

writing.meaning:
n. 书写, 著作, 笔迹, 作品
[医] 书写

Only later did she discover a talent for writing.
I wanted to try out a new style of writing.
definition: n. the act of creating written works
n. the work of a writer; anything expressed in letters of the alphabet (especially when considered from the point of view of style and effect)

wrong.meaning:
a. 错误的, 不正当的, 失常的
adv. 错误地
examples: I got all the answers wrong.
He was driving on the wrong side of the road.
Sorry, I must have dialled the wrong number.

yacht.meaning:
n. 快艇, 游艇
vi. 驾游艇, 乘游艇

yard.meaning:
n. 码, 庭院, 工场
[化] 堆置场

My next-door neighbor was watering her yard.

yawn.meaning:
n. 哈欠
vi. 打哈欠, 裂开
vt. 打着哈欠说

We couldn't help yawning during the speech.

year.meaning:
n. 年, 年度, 年龄
[经] 年度

I lost my job earlier this year.

yearly.meaning:
a. 每年的, 一年一度的
adv. 一年一次, 每年

yearn.meaning: vi. 渴望, 想念, 怀念, 同情

yearning.meaning:
n. 渴望, 热望, 怀念
a. 热望的, 渴望的, 怀念的, 向往的

yell.meaning:

vt. 喊叫着说

yellow.meaning:
n. 黄色
a. 黄色的

v. turn yellow

yes.meaning:
adv. 是
n. 是, 同意

yet.meaning:
adv. 还, 尚, 仍然, 已经, 然而
conj. 然而

yield.meaning:

yogurt.meaning:
n. 酸乳酪

young.meaning:

youthful.meaning:
a. 年轻的, 青年的

yummy.meaning: a. 美味的, 可口的, 赏心悦目的, 愉快的

zeal.meaning: n. 热心, 热衷, 热诚

zero.meaning:

abbreviation.meaning: n. 缩写词, 缩写, 缩短, 节略

abolition.meaning:

abundance.meaning:

[计] 计算器
examples: I used the calculator app on my phone.
Exam candidates are not allowed to use advanced calculators with database capability.
The flexible savings account has an online calculator that helps employees estimate health expenses.
definition: n. an expert at calculation (or at operating calculating machines)
n. a small machine that is used for mathematical calculations

cancellation.meaning:
n. 取消, 作废, 注销戳
[经] 注销, 取消, 保险单的注销
examples: We need at least 24 hours' notice of cancellation.
Heavy seas can cause cancellation of ferry services.
Cancellations must be made in writing.
definition: n. the act of cancelling; calling off some arrangement
n. the speech act of revoking or annulling or making void

candidacy.meaning:
n. 候选人的地位, 候选资格
[法] 候选人的身份, 资格
examples: She is expected to announce officially her candidacy for president early next week.
He waited until the end of August to announce his candidacy.
definition: n the campaign of a candidate to be elected

candidate.meaning:
n. 候选人, 投考者
[法] 候选, 候补者
examples: He is the best candidate for the job.
She stood as a candidate in the local elections.
The party is fielding more candidates than ever before.
definition: n. someone who is considered for something (for an office or prize or honor etc.)

capability.meaning:
n. 能力, 性能, 约束力
[化] 能力
examples: Age affects the range of a person's capabilities.
She has the capability to become a very fine actor.
Animals in the zoo have lost the capability of catching food for themselves.
definition: n. the quality of being capable -- physically or intellectually or legally
n. the susceptibility of something to a particular treatment

capitalism.meaning:
n. 资本主义
[经] 资本主义
examples: The former communist embraced capitalism and started his own company.
She wrote that capitalism was devastating the environment.
Their form of conservatism stresses limited government, free-market capitalism and personal responsibility.
definition: n. an economic system based on private ownership of capital

capitalist.meaning:
n. 资本家, 资本主义者
a. 资本主义的
examples: Many of these capitalists have been able to benefit from privatization.
She writes that the capitalist system has never worked for the poor.
He is broadly perceived as a free-market capitalist.
definition: n. a conservative advocate of capitalism
n. a person who invests capital in a business (especially a large business)

captivity.meaning:
n. 囚禁, 被关
[法] 囚禁, 被俘, 俘虏
examples: He was held in captivity for three years.
Wild animals do not always breed well in captivity.
The bird had escaped from captivity.
definition: n. the state of being imprisoned

carbohydrate.meaning:
n. 碳水化合物, 糖类
[化] 糖类; 碳水化合物
examples: Nuts are high in carbohydrates.
I'm trying to cut down on carbohydrates.
Eat your carbohydrates within two hours after your workout.
definition: n. an essential structural component of living cells and source of energy for animals; includes simple sugars with small molecules as well as macromolecular substances; are classified according to the number of monosaccharide groups they contain

cardboard.meaning:
n. 薄纸板
[化] 咭纸; 特等纸板; 卡纸板; 卡片纸板

s. without substance

carefully.meaning: adv. 小心地, 谨慎地
examples: Drive carefully.
She put the glass down carefully.
Please listen carefully.

definition: n. the quality of not being careful or taking pains

examples: A master carpenter was in charge of teaching the apprentices.
He was apprenticed to a carpenter at the age of sixteen.

definition: n. a woodworker who makes or repairs wooden objects
v. work as a carpenter

catastrophe.meaning:
n. 大灾难, 大祸
[化] 突变

The attempt to expand the business was a catastrophe for the firm.
We've had a few catastrophes with the food for the party.

n. a sudden violent change in the earth's surface

catastrophic.meaning: a. 悲惨的, 灾难的
examples: An unchecked increase in the use of fossil fuels could have catastrophic results for the planet.
A catastrophic storm made landfall on U.S. soil.
She had to put her catastrophic Olympic performance out of her mind.

celebrate.meaning: v. 庆祝, 祝贺, 举行
examples: Jake's passed his exams. We're going out to celebrate.
We had good reason to celebrate.

I hope you'll join in the Christmas celebrations.

n. any joyous diversion

examples: He became a celebrity in China after winning a gold medal at the Olympics.

definition: n. a widely known person

censorship.meaning:
n. 检查制度
[医] 督察, 监察

The government has imposed strict censorship on the press.
Civil libertarians say that the ruling amounts to censorship.

n deleting parts of publications or correspondence or theatrical performances

centralize.meaning:
vt. 集聚, 集中, 施行中央集权

ceremonial.meaning:
n. 仪式

certainty.meaning:
n. 确定, 确实的事情
[法] 确定, 肯定, 必然的事

certificate.meaning:
n. 证书, 证明书

challenge.meaning:

challenging.meaning: a. 挑战的, 引起争论的
examples: I have had a challenging and rewarding career as a teacher.

champagne.meaning:
n. 香槟酒, 香槟酒色
[化] 香槟酒

We always celebrate our wedding anniversary with a bottle of champagne.

championship.meaning: n. 冠军身份, 冠军称号, 捍卫

n. a competition at which a champion is chosen

chancellor.meaning: n. 大臣, 总理, 首相, 大使馆/领事馆的一等秘书, 司法官, 大学校长
examples: The talks were headed by Germany's Chancellor Merkel.
MPs waited for the chancellor's announcement.

character.meaning:
n. 个性, 字符, 人物, 性质, 品格, 资格

characterize.meaning: vt. 描绘...的特性, 刻划...的性格

charitable.meaning:
a. 大慈大悲的, 宽厚的, 慈善的
[法] 慈善的, 慷慨的, 宽恕的

a. full of love and generosity

chemistry.meaning:
n. 化学, 化学过程

childbirth.meaning:
n. 分娩

childhood.meaning:
n. 孩童时期

chocolate.meaning:
n. 巧克力
a. 巧克力制的

cholesterol.meaning:
n. 胆固醇

christian.meaning:
n. 基督徒, 正派人

chronicle.meaning:

circulation.meaning:

citizenship.meaning:

n. 重新洗牌, 改组, 撤换

residence.meaning:

resignation.meaning:

resounding.meaning: a. 响亮的, 轰动的

resourceful.meaning:
